(16 goals each) | matches = 210 | total goals = 548 | average attendance = 14,984 | prevseason = [[2001 Chinese Jia-A League|2001]] | nextseason = [[2003 Chinese Jia-A League|2003]] }} The '''2002 [[Chinese Jia-A League]] season''' was the ninth season of professional association football and the 41st top-tier overall league season in China. The league started on March 9 and ended on November 30, with [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] winning the championship. In order to help the [[China national football team|Chinese national team]] prepare for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], there was no relegation within the league for this season. ==Promotion and relegation== '''Teams promoted from 2001 Jia-B League''' *[[Beijing Chengfeng F.C.|Shanghai Zhongyuan Huili]] '''Teams relegated to 2002 Jia-B League''' *None ==Overview== Before the league started it was dogged by rumours of match fixing when it was discovered that second tier club and promotion hopeful [[Changchun Yatai F.C.|Changchun Yatai]] had [[2001 Chinese football match-fixing scandal|fixed a match on October 6, 2001]] against [[Zhejiang Professional F.C.|Zhejiang]] in their favour. When these allegations turned out to be true, Changchun Yatai were denied promotion into the league as their punishment, which meant there would only be 15 teams performing within the league.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesc/china01.html China 2001] at rsssf.org 19 Jun 2003 Retrieved 08-01-2013 Also before the season started it was decided that because the [[China national football team|Chinese national team]] had qualified for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], there would be no relegation so the players would not be distracted with the fear of demotion. Within the season [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] would continue their dominance within Chinese football and win their third consecutive league championship.[http://zuqiuziliao.cn/china/2002a.htm 2002甲A] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720214606/http://zuqiuziliao.cn/china/2002a.htm |date=2012-07-20 }} at zuqiuziliao.cn 2011-07-14 Retrieved 08-01-2013 ==Personnel== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:95%" |- !Team !Manager |- | [[Bayi Football Team|August 1st]] | |- | [[Beijing Guoan F.C.|Beijing Guoan]] | {{flagicon|SCG}} [[Ljupko Petrović]] |- | [[Guangzhou City F.C.|Changsha Ginde]] | {{flagicon|POR}} [[Toni (footballer, born 1946)|Toni]] |- | [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]] | {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Edson Tavares]] |- | [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] | {{flagicon|FRY}} [[Milorad Kosanović]] |- | [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning Bird]] | {{flagicon|CHN}} [[Wang Hongli (footballer)|Wang Hongli]] |- | [[Qingdao Hainiu F.C.|Qingdao Hademen]] | {{flagicon|KOR}} [[Lee Jang-soo]] |- | [[Harbin Guoli F.C.|Shaanxi Guoli]] | |- | [[Shandong Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] | {{flagicon|RUS}} [[Valery Nepomnyashchy]] |- | [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]] | {{flagicon|CHN}} [[Wu Jingui]] |- | [[Beijing Chengfeng F.C.|Shanghai Zhongyuan Huili]] | {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Claude Le Roy]] |- | [[Shenzhen F.C.|Shenzhen Ping'an Insurance]] | {{flagicon|CHN}} [[Zhu Guanghu]] |- | [[Sichuan First City F.C.|Sichuan Dahe]] | |- | [[Tianjin Jinmen Tiger F.C.|Tianjin TEDA]] | {{flagicon|URU}} [[Nelson Agresta]] |- | [[Yunnan Hongta F.C.|Yunnan Hongta]] | {{flagicon|CHN}} [[Qi Wusheng]] |} ==Foreign players== As a military-owned team, August 1st were not allowed to sign any foreign players. {|class="wikitable" !
